query: Starting from a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, what single intervention could overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength? The hypothesis should address the tendency for dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries to produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage during straining. Specify the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted strength and ductility relative to the untreated starting material, the applicable testing and operating conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) can overcome the limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness of a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies while retaining or increasing strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies
generation.conditions: Room temperature, quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests
generation.structural_mediator: Hierarchical microstructure with a skeletal, non-recrystallized B2 phase and a recrystallized FCC phase
generation.mechanism: PSR eliminates weak boundaries, prevents premature crack nucleation, and allows both phases to contribute to strain hardening simultaneously through high-density dislocation multiplication and a strain-induced B2 to BCT phase transformation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved tensile ductility and strength, with a uniform elongation of ~30% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ~2.2 GPa
generation.baseline: As-cast alloy with limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness
generation.boundary: The PSR strategy may not be effective if the material undergoes extended annealing toward uniform grains or if the alloy has high stacking fault energy
generation.uncertainty: Theoretical model for calculating the suitable deformation level for PSR is semi-quantitative and ignores information on microstructure and strain rate

falsification_experiment.design: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the PSR-treated alloy does not exhibit improved tensile ductility and strength compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

Question: How does the capacity for twinning-controlled deformation in the equiatomic CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy generate a simultaneous increase in strength and ductility, and what is the origin of its exceptional fracture toughness?. System: Nominally equiatomic CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy (MEA) with a single-phase face-centered cubic (fcc) structure. Processing: Samples extracted from a previously produced alloy; micro-pillars (~300 nm diameter) machined using focused-ion beam (FIB) techniques; in situ TEM compression tests performed at 300 kV; in situ TEM tensile tests conducted at room temperature using a Gatan model 654 single-tilt straining holder at 200 kV; DFT calculations performed using VASP with the nudged-elastic band method. Test conditions: Room temperature (300 K); uniaxial tension and compression; micro-pillar compression at 300 kV; in situ straining at 10 frames per second; DFT calculations at 0 K and 500 K. Question: How can a single-phase face-centered cubic medium-entropy alloy achieve both gigapascal yield strength and high uniform ductility without relying on second-phase heterogeneities?. System: Equimolar CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy (33.48Cr-32.46Co-34.06Ni atomic percent). Processing: Electromagnetic levitation melting, homogenization at 1,473 K for 12 h, hot forging (1,323–1,173 K), cold rolling to 0.5 mm sheets, followed by partial recrystallization annealing at 873 K for 1 h and water quenching. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at strain rate 5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, room temperature (298 K) and liquid nitrogen temperature (77 K); loading-unloading-reloading (LUR) tests to measure back stresses. Findings: Yield strength (σ0.2) of ~1,150 MPa achieved with a three-level heterogeneous grain structure (HGS) spanning nanometer to micrometer scales.; Uniform tensile strain (Eu) reached 22% at room temperature, significantly higher than the ~2% Eu observed in homogeneous ultrafine-grained counterparts with similar strength.; The number density of nanograins (ρNG) increased from 4.7 grains/µm² before testing to 21 grains/µm² after deformation at 298 K and 31 gra

Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement. Findings: The phase-selectively recrystallized (PSR) EHEA achieves a uniform elongation of ∼33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ∼2.2 GPa.; The PSR EHEA exhibits a fracture true strain of ∼30%, which is double that of the As-cast (AC) alloy (∼14%) and the fully recrystallized (FR) alloy (∼17%).; The fracture true stress of the PSR EHEA reaches ∼1850 MPa, significantly higher than the AC (∼1390 MPa) and FR (∼1460 MPa)
